The Problem

Braille literacy
is priced out of reach.

$2,500+
Average cost of a commercial Refreshable Braille Display
"Less than 10% of visually impaired individuals in developing countries have access to a Braille device. Price is the primary barrier."

Existing tools depend on slow cloud APIs, require constant internet, and lack the adaptive intelligence to handle the modern web — let alone teach Braille from scratch.

↳ The Tacura Answer

An affordable, high-speed, offline-capable haptic terminal. It learns from the user, browses the web through a semantic AI agent, and accepts Braille chord input — all on a $35 Raspberry Pi.

  • ✓Servo-based 6-dot Braille cell — no pneumatics, no piezo
  • ✓Faster-Whisper STT + Piper TTS — fully local voice pipeline
  • ✓Groq-accelerated Llama 3.1 — <1s web summarization
  • ✓Adaptive curriculum with mastery tracking + confusion drills
Product Features

Three pillars.
One terminal.

01 / LEARN
🧠

Interactive AI Tutor

An adaptive engine powered by Groq (Llama 3.1) and stateful memory. Tacura listens, evaluates spoken Braille, tracks per-letter mastery, and runs confusion-pair drills in real time. Level 0 through Level 4 — from cell orientation to sentence fluency.

faster-whisper Piper TTS Groq LLM
02 / TYPE
⌨️

Perkins-Style Chord Input

An 11-button workstation for chorded Braille typing. Dots 1–6 combine simultaneously to produce any Grade 1 character. A release-triggered Arduino engine captures the full chord before firing — enabling natural finger placement and zero mis-fires.

Release-triggered 11 buttons C++ chord engine
03 / BROWSE
🌐

Semantic Web Agent

Type any query in Braille. Tacura fetches live search results, extracts clean text via Trafilatura, and distils it into 3–5 Braille-friendly sentences under 60 characters each. The summary streams to the haptic cell letter by letter in under 5 seconds.

DuckDuckGo Trafilatura Edge AI
Technical Architecture

Built on open hardware.
Powered by edge AI.

Python and C++ on a Pi 3B+. Faster-Whisper for local voice recognition. Groq-optimized Llama 3 for lightning-fast semantic reasoning. An Arduino bridge controls SG90 servos with sub-50ms haptic response.

FIG. 1 — Software pipeline: Voice → STT → LLM → Haptic
FIG. 2 — Circuit schematic (Tinkercad) — 4.5V servo rail, Arduino Uno
🎙️

Speech Recognition

Offline STT via faster-whisper tiny with Silero VAD filter. Latency <4s on Pi 3B+. Extracts single Braille letters from natural speech.

🔊

Neural Text-to-Speech

Piper TTS with en_US-lessac-low model. Runs real-time on Pi. Binary PCM pipe to aplay for zero-latency audio.

⚡

AI Reasoning

Groq API (free tier) running llama-3.1-8b-instant. 14,400 req/day free. Stateful learner profile JSON passed per call.

🤖

Haptic Bridge

Arduino Uno receives letter commands via serial at 9600 baud. Holds servo pattern until next command. Sub-50ms response.

🌐

Web Agent

DuckDuckGo Lite → Trafilatura extraction → Groq summarization. Pipeline runs async in background. First haptic character in <5s.

The Prototype

From cardboard to
classroom-ready.

PROTOTYPE v1.1

Built in 15 days for the AMD Slingshot Hackathon, Bhopal. The prototype uses 18650 Li-ion cells, a buck converter for regulated 5V servo power, and a hand-fabricated Braille cell with 6 SG90 servos mounted in a 2×3 grid.

  • ComputeRaspberry Pi 3B+ · 1GB RAM
  • ControllerArduino Uno (Serial slave)
  • Haptic Output6× SG90 servo · 2×3 grid
  • Servo Latency<50ms per character
  • STT Latency~4s (VAD-filtered)
  • Power2× 18650 · DC buck 5V rail
  • OSRaspberry Pi OS Lite · headless
  • Build Cost~₹6,500 ($78 USD)
  • Market Equivalent$2,500+
